question: Should OpenClaw deliberately reject already-configured unmanaged Codex app-server versions newer than 0.144.5 until their generated protocol schemas are validated and adopted?
rationale: This is an intentional fail-closed compatibility change for existing `appServer.command` and external control-socket users; source review cannot determine whether the stricter upgrade policy is the desired product contract.

options.title: Keep the validated ceiling
options.body: Retain the 0.144.5 upper bound and add upgrade-oriented proof that a newer custom app-server receives clear remediation guidance.

options.title: Allow newer versions provisionally
options.body: Preserve current custom-version behavior until a later schema-validation mechanism can safely distinguish compatible newer releases.

options.title: Restrict the ceiling to managed runtime
options.body: Enforce the exact generated-schema range for OpenClaw-managed Codex while separately deciding the policy for explicitly configured external servers.

recommendation.title: Keep the validated ceiling
recommendation.body: Retain the 0.144.5 upper bound and add upgrade-oriented proof that a newer custom app-server receives clear remediation guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The available release provenance and assignment connect steipete to the original bundled Codex app-server harness and this proposed compatibility boundary.
